findings.issue: No test infrastructure at all: no test script, no vitest/playwright devDependency, no spec files in app/.
findings.suggestion: Add vitest and a small suite for lib/format.ts and the route loaders; loaders are plain async functions and React Router v8's createRoutesStub covers component-level tests without a server.

findings.issue: The riskiest logic in the app — three filters, id<=10000 alternate-form exclusion, page clamp (Math.min) and slice — has no regression guard; an off-by-one would shift every page silently.
findings.suggestion: Extract filtering/pagination into a pure function and unit-test boundary cases: page beyond total, page=0, NaN, unknown type param, empty results, exactly 48 matches.

findings.issue: Debounced URL-state sync (replace:true, page reset on filter change, stale searchParams closure) is untested and easy to break with a small refactor.
findings.suggestion: Test via createRoutesStub or Playwright component tests that typing updates q after the debounce, resets page to 1, and preserves other filters.

findings.issue: compareRows' missing-sorts-last-in-both-directions semantics and the level-up/machine/egg/tutor method ordering are subtle spec behaviors with no test pinning them.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test compareRows directly (ascending/descending with null values) and the method-ordering comparator against representative inputs.

findings.issue: All pure helpers are trivially testable and encode spec edge cases (mr-mime→'Mr Mime', \f collapse, '—' for null power, #0025 padding) yet are untested.
findings.suggestion: A 30-line vitest file over format.ts is the cheapest, highest-value addition to this codebase.

findings.issue: Alternate-form exclusion and dedupe are reimplemented inline here while cardsFromRefs (data.server.ts:113) has its own copy; neither copy is pinned by a test, so they can silently diverge, including the hidden-ability merge.
findings.suggestion: Route ability card building through cardsFromRefs (extended to carry the hidden flag) and test it once, including a Pokémon listed both normally and as hidden.

findings.issue: Promise cache deletes rejected entries so failures aren't sticky — correct but fragile under refactor, and untested.
findings.suggestion: Add a unit test asserting a failed fetch is retried on the next call and a succeeded one is cached.

findings.issue: Loaders return { notFound: true } flags instead of throwing 404 Responses, so HTTP status is never 404 and no test documents the not-found contract.
findings.suggestion: Throw a 404 Response via the framework's isRouteErrorResponse path (root.tsx already imports it) and add one loader test per route for the missing-resource case.

findings.issue: latestEnglishFlavorText skips empty English entries while the spec says take the last English entry — a quiet divergence a unit test would have surfaced.
findings.suggestion: Pin the spec behavior (or the intentional deviation) in a test with fixture entries.

findings.issue: Type moves are sorted by humanized display name where the spec says 'sorted alphabetically by name'; usually identical, occasionally not, and untested.
findings.suggestion: Sort by API name (or test that display-name and API-name orders agree on the shipped data).

summary: The app shipped zero tests of its own: no test script, no runner, no spec files, leaving the provided acceptance suite as the only guard. That's costly here because the logic most likely to rot — home filtering/pagination, URL-state debouncing, move-table sorting with missing-values-last semantics, and duplicated alternate-form/hidden-ability handling — is dense, subtle, and spec-pinned. React Router v8 makes testing cheap (plain async loaders plus createRoutesStub), so a small vitest suite over format.ts and the extracted loader logic is the highest-leverage improvement this PR could still make.
